posts.title: Farewell, ESO
posts.description: I’ve done a lot of posts and videos about the Elder Scrolls Online over the years [almost 8], but I finally reached a point where I didn’t want to play any more, not even to visit some of my favourite builds. So today I took a deep breath and deleted all my game files. I thought it would hurt more…but Pete Seeger was right: Pete Seeger did write this song but he isn’t performing it because, well, I just like this version better. Cheers, Meeks

posts.title: Social Media HELP for Parents
posts.description: Here in Australia, we’ve initiated age controls to protect kids younger than 16 from some of the most harmful content on social media, including Youtube. But what of little kids and tweens? Yes there are things parents can do to protect their kids, but the pressure from Youtube’s own algorithms is far too great for individual parents to fight. And whenever the subject of regulation arises on social media, the comment section is flooded with self-righteous people whose mantra is: ‘it’s the parent’s job to supervise their kids’. The irony of those comments is that none of these people have kids of their own AND what they really mean is ‘don’t inconvenience me with nasty regulations’. Now, finally, Hank Green and a cohort of parents have joined forces to create a version of Youtube that is made specifically for young kids. It’s curated by parents, and it is educational. posts.title: Physics for Scifi
posts.description: I love science fiction, but I hate scifi solutions that are more magic than science. For that reason, I don’t often read military science fiction that requires space ships to travel faster than the speed of light, or ‘warp’ from one spot to another, or… float down to a planet using anti-gravity. And now, finally, a lay person’s video about why all of that scifi magic is rubbish! I don’t have the physics background or the math to follow the nitty gritty parts of this video – I have to take them on trust – but I’ve always loved geometry so the underlying concepts make perfect sense to me. As humans we have this ingrained belief that we can engineer anything…given enough time and resources. And I’m not completely immune to that bias either, so maybe someone, some when, will find a loophole against gravity to exploit, but it’s not looking good. I hope fellow scifi fans will find something of interest here. Cheers, Meeks
